speaker: Unknown
en: For his first 50 years, Sam Walton was not at all a national figure.
zh: 在他人生的头50年里，山姆·沃尔顿完全不是全国知名人物。

speaker: Unknown
en: He remained in the shadows off the beaten track.
zh: 他一直隐身于人迹罕至之处。

speaker: Unknown
en: It was only in the early 1980s that a startled public discovered that the richest man in America was not a Rockefeller, a DuPont, a Trump, a Kennedy, a Getty, or a Perot, but an unglamorous guy from Arkansas named Sam Walton.
zh: 直到1980年代初，公众才震惊地发现，美国首富并非洛克菲勒、杜邦、特朗普、肯尼迪、盖蒂或佩罗，而是一个来自阿肯色州、名叫山姆·沃尔顿的其貌不扬的家伙。

speaker: Unknown
en: Reporters discovered that he was ordinary, that he grew up in Missouri in the Depression, worked his way through college, lived a clean Christian life, served stateside in World War II, married an Oklahoma banker's daughter, opened up his first five and dime store in Backwater, North Central Arkansas, and raised four healthy kids.
zh: 记者们发现他很平凡：他在大萧条时期的密苏里州长大，靠打工读完大学，过着纯净的基督徒生活，二战期间在美国本土服役，娶了俄克拉荷马州一位银行家的女儿，在阿肯色州中北部的小镇巴克沃特开了他的第一家五分一毛店，养大了四个健康的孩子。

speaker: Unknown
en: Pretty darned ordinary.
zh: 相当平凡。

speaker: Unknown
en: But only on the surface.
zh: 但这只是表面。

speaker: Unknown
en: Sam Walton underneath was no ordinary man.
zh: 山姆·沃尔顿的内在绝非凡人之辈。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's one of my favorite paragraphs in the book I'm going to talk to you about today, which is Sam Walton, the inside story of America's richest man, and it was written by Vance Trimble.
zh: 这是我今天要跟你讲的这本书里我最喜欢的一段话，这本书就是《山姆·沃尔顿：美国首富的内幕故事》，作者是万斯·特里姆布尔。

speaker: Unknown
en: So this book is almost 40 years old.
zh: 这本书已经差不多40年了。

speaker: Unknown
en: It was actually written before Sam's famous autobiography made it in America.
zh: 它实际上是在山姆那本著名自传在美国出版之前写的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And what I want to do, this is like the third or fourth time that I read the book.
zh: 我想做的是——这已经是我第三次或第四次读这本书了。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I just want to run through a bunch of ideas that are mainly focused less on like his early life in the biography, but more about how he essentially worked and how he thought about building his business.
zh: 所以我只想过一遍一堆想法，主要不是聚焦于传记中他的早年生活，而更多是关于他实际上是如何工作的，以及他如何看待打造自己的生意。

speaker: Unknown
en: I want to jump into the fact that this is one of the most important paragraphs, I think, of the book because it's an illustration of Charlie Munger's great idea, which is like you should find a simple idea and take it very seriously.
zh: 我想直接跳到我认为是书中最重要的一段话之一，因为它印证了查理·芒格的一个伟大观点，那就是：你应该找到一个简单的理念，并极其认真地对待它。

speaker: Unknown
en: So it says to him, making money was only a game, a test of his imagination and expertise to see how far he could drive a business concept.
zh: 书里说，对他而言，赚钱只是一场游戏，是对他的想象力和专业能力的一种测试，看他能把一个商业概念推进到多远。

speaker: Unknown
en: Wall Street had a hard time getting the drift of that.
zh: 华尔街很难领会这层意思。

speaker: Unknown
en: Sam's idea, he admitted, was absurdly simple.
zh: 山姆承认，他的想法简单得近乎荒谬。

speaker: Unknown
en: Buy cheap, sell low, every day, and while doing it with a smile.
zh: 买得便宜，卖得低廉，每一天如此，并且做这一切时面带微笑。

speaker: Unknown
en: Then it goes into the fact that he, just like Henry Singleton, you and I talked about Henry Singleton a few weeks ago.
zh: 接着书里讲到，他和亨利·辛格尔顿一样——几周前我和你聊过亨利·辛格尔顿。

speaker: Unknown
en: Singleton was criticized because by a lot of people who said, oh, you don't have like, you know, a five-year, 10-year, 15-year business plan.
zh: 辛格尔顿曾被很多人批评，他们说他，哦，你没有那种五年、十年、十五年的商业计划。

speaker: Unknown
en: Michael Bloomberg last week was the exact same way.
zh: 上周的迈克尔·布隆伯格也是完全一样。

speaker: Unknown
en: Sam Walton was also the same way.
zh: 山姆·沃尔顿同样如此。

speaker: Unknown
en: He just wanted to wake up every day, work on Walmart, and then he was fine with changing his mind.
zh: 他只是想每天醒来，做沃尔玛的事，然后他完全乐于改变主意。

speaker: Unknown
en: Over and over again in the book, he'll be presented with new information.
zh: 书中一次又一次地出现这样的情节：他会接触到新信息。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like, okay, I was going left, new information, I'm going to go right.
zh: 比如，好吧，我本来要往左走，有了新信息，我要往右走。

speaker: Unknown
en: So he was a genius in business with an iron mind, unwilling to compromise any of his carefully thought out principles.
zh: 所以他是商业天才，有着钢铁般的意志，不愿妥协任何经过深思熟虑的原则。

speaker: Unknown
en: But Sam Walton is flexible.
zh: 但山姆·沃尔顿是灵活的。

speaker: Unknown
en: If he adopts a business course that doesn't work out, he's neither too vain nor too blind to see his mistake, to say so and to change his heading 180 degrees.
zh: 如果他采用的一条商业路线行不通，他既不会因为太虚荣，也不会因为太盲目而看不到自己的错误，他会承认错误，并把航向调整180度。

speaker: Unknown
en: Another principle that recurs throughout the book is the fact that he did not like attention.
zh: 书中反复出现的另一个原则是，他不喜欢受到关注。

speaker: Unknown
en: He'd rather just wake up, work on his business.
zh: 他宁愿只是醒来，做自己的生意。

speaker: Unknown
en: He was greatly disturbed.
zh: 他深受困扰。

speaker: Unknown
en: It says when Ford Magazine set him at the top of their list of America's 400 richest Americans, this disturbed him greatly.
zh: 书里说，当《福特杂志》把他列在美国400位首富榜单的顶端时，这让他大为不安。

speaker: Unknown
en: He granted very few interviews.
zh: 他极少接受采访。

speaker: Unknown
en: He turned his back on most TV cameras.
zh: 他背对大多数电视摄像机。

speaker: Unknown
en: He shuddered each time another magazine piece appeared.
zh: 每当又一篇杂志报道出现，他都会不寒而栗。

speaker: Unknown
en: One of the most interesting things about Sam Walton is that he had insanely high energy levels.
zh: 关于山姆·沃尔顿最有趣的几点之一是，他拥有极其旺盛的精力。

speaker: Unknown
en: In fact, a friend of mine just sent me this great post on Napoleon, and I want to read this to you real quick, and I think it applies to Sam Walton as well.
zh: 事实上，我的一个朋友刚给我发了一篇关于拿破仑的精彩帖子，我想快速读给你听，我认为它同样适用于山姆·沃尔顿。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the post says, it will never not be funny to me that when Napoleon got stripped of his empire and exiled, he responded by paving the roads, draining marshes, rebuilding the iron mines, and ordered every house to install a toilet in just two months.
zh: 帖子说：让我永远觉得好笑的是，当拿破仑被剥夺帝国并遭流放时，他的回应是铺路、排干沼泽、重建铁矿，并下令每户人家在短短两个月内安装一个马桶。

speaker: Unknown
en: Energy is a choice, he said.
zh: 精力是一种选择，他说。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is Sam Walton in high school.
zh: 这是高中时期的山姆·沃尔顿。

speaker: Unknown
en: He was going out for football and basketball, learning to play tennis, making A's and making friends, grinding away on the merit badges in hopes of becoming an Eagle Scout, regularly attending Sunday school and scrambling after every odd job that would put money in his pocket.
zh: 他参加橄榄球和篮球运动，学习打网球，拿A、交朋友，努力争取荣誉徽章以期成为鹰级童子军，定期参加主日学校，并且抢着做一切能让他口袋里有钱的零工。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is what his dad said about how he raised his sons.
zh: 这是他的父亲谈到他如何养育儿子时说的。

speaker: Unknown
en: The secret is work, work, work.
zh: 秘诀就是工作，工作，再工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: I taught the boys how to do it.
zh: 是我教会了男孩们怎么干。

speaker: Unknown
en: Sam's father was a bear for work and he would not tolerate sons who were not likewise industrious, ambitious, and decent.
zh: 山姆的父亲是个工作狂，他绝不容忍儿子们不同样勤奋、有抱负、正直。

speaker: Unknown
en: This continues.
zh: 书里接着写道。

speaker: Unknown
en: Sam was the quarterback of the football team, also played on the basketball team, was the president of the student body, and he was in just about every club and organization.
zh: 山姆是橄榄球队的四分卫，也在篮球队打球，是学生会主席，而且他几乎参加了每一个社团和组织。

speaker: Unknown
en: He was active.
zh: 他非常活跃。

speaker: Unknown
en: Sam was a hard worker.
zh: 山姆是个勤奋工作的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: He was optimistic all the time.
zh: 他一直都很乐观。

speaker: Unknown
en: He had a great smile on his face and felt like everybody was his friend and that the world was something that he could conquer.
zh: 他脸上总挂着灿烂的笑容，觉得人人都是他的朋友，觉得世界是他可以征服的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: He just didn't waste time.
zh: 他只是不浪费时间。

speaker: Unknown
en: He was always busy doing something.
zh: 他总是忙于做某件事。

speaker: Unknown
en: And one of the most interesting parts of the book is the fact that Sam, it's not like he set out for a career in retail.
zh: 这本书最有趣的部分之一是，Sam 并不是一开始就立志从事零售业的。

speaker: Unknown
en: In fact, after he graduated school, he had no idea what he wanted to be.
zh: 事实上，他毕业后完全不知道自己想做什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: At one point, he's like, oh, maybe I'll be the president of the United States.
zh: 有一次，他说，哦，也许我会当美国总统。

speaker: Unknown
en: But he decides he needs to make money, so he interviews for a job at the retail store, JCPenney.
zh: 但他决定自己需要赚钱，所以他去了一家零售店 JCPenney 面试。

speaker: Unknown
en: And this is really important because there's a lot of ideas that he learned at JCPenney that he's gonna use for the next 50 years of his own career.
zh: 这一点非常重要，因为他在 JCPenney 学到的很多理念，将在他自己接下来 50 年的职业生涯中派上用场。

speaker: Unknown
en: So he says, I interviewed a JCPenney and I liked what I heard.
zh: 所以他说，我面试了 JCPenney，我喜欢我听到的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: They offered me a job at $85 a month.
zh: 他们给我开了一份月薪 85 美元的工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: Sam Walton plunged into this new world of merchandising with the keen and furious dedication of a quarterback who was one touchdown behind with two minutes to go.
zh: Sam Walton 以一个落后一个达阵、只剩两分钟的四分卫那种敏锐而狂热的投入，一头扎进了这个全新的商品零售世界。

speaker: Unknown
en: Sam Walton knew little of the scope of the JCPenney company chain and absolutely no details of the personality and meteoric rise of the old man himself.
zh: Sam Walton 对 JCPenney 这家公司连锁帝国的规模知之甚少，对老先生本人的个性和火箭般的崛起更是毫无了解。

speaker: Unknown
en: He would learn more soon, including one profitable lesson taught to him personally by John Cash Penny.
zh: 他很快就会了解更多，包括 John Cash Penney 亲自教给他的一堂受益匪浅的课。

speaker: Unknown
en: The founder, who was then age 65.
zh: 这位创始人当时 65 岁。

speaker: Unknown
en: In fact, Sam would borrow JCPenney's whole concept of how to succeed by putting customer satisfaction ahead of profits.
zh: 事实上，Sam 将会借鉴 JCPenney 的整个成功理念：把顾客满意度放在利润之前。

speaker: Unknown
en: And at the time that Sam was working for him, it's a massive chain.
zh: 而 Sam 为他工作的时候，这已经是一家庞大的连锁企业。

speaker: Unknown
en: It has over 1,500 stores and sales are running at over $300 million.
zh: 它拥有超过 1,500 家门店，销售额超过 3 亿美元。

speaker: Unknown
en: That is in 1940.
zh: 那是在 1940 年。

speaker: Unknown
en: And one thing that Sam learned was that the company's strength, meaning JCPenney, was in these small towns and small cities, an idea he's gonna later adopt when he starts Walmart.
zh: Sam 学到的一件事是，公司(也就是 JCPenney)的优势在于这些小镇和小城市——这是他后来创办 Walmart 时会采纳的理念。

speaker: Unknown
en: And this is one of Sam Walton's favorite stories about JCPenney.
zh: 这是 Sam Walton 最喜欢的关于 JCPenney 的故事之一。

speaker: Unknown
en: JCPenney himself arrived in town and spent a lot of time wandering around the store.
zh: JCPenney 本人来到镇上，花了很多时间在店里四处走动。

speaker: Unknown
en: Sam Walton would do exactly this later on.
zh: Sam Walton 后来也会做完全一样的事。

speaker: Unknown
en: A customer came in and bought something from Sam, and while he wrapped it for her, JCPenney was observing the transaction closely.
zh: 一位顾客进来从 Sam 那里买了东西，在他为她包装的时候，JCPenney 正密切观察着这笔交易。

speaker: Unknown
en: After the customer left, Mr. Penney came over and said, boys, I want to show you something.
zh: 顾客离开后，Penney 先生走过来，说，孩子们，我要给你们看点东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: And he took a box about the same size and he went around it with paper and let it overlap, maybe a quarter of an inch.
zh: 他拿了一个差不多大小的盒子，用纸把它包起来，让纸重叠大约四分之一英寸。

speaker: Unknown
en: Then he went around it with twine one time like this and one time like that, and then he tied it.
zh: 然后他用绳子绕一圈像这样，再绕一圈像那样，然后把它系上。

speaker: Unknown
en: He said, boys, you know we don't make a dime out of the merchandise we sell.
zh: 他说，孩子们，你们知道吗，我们卖的商品本身一分钱都赚不到。

speaker: Unknown
en: We only make our profit out of the paper and string that we save.
zh: 我们的利润只来自我们节省下来的纸和绳。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then another idea that Sam's going to borrow and copy when he does Walmart and even before in the early days of the stores that he owns is aligning the incentives and making sure that the managers of each store have essentially unlimited upside that they can make a lot of money depending on how the sales and profitability of their stores are.
zh: 然后 Sam 在做 Walmart 时、甚至更早在他拥有自己门店的早期，还会借鉴和复制的另一个理念是：对齐激励机制，确保每家店的经理拥有本质上无上限的上行空间，也就是说，根据他们门店的销售额和盈利能力，他们可以赚到很多钱。

speaker: Unknown
en: So it says, in Sam's memory, those days are still vivid.
zh: 书里写道，在 Sam 的记忆里，那些日子依然鲜活。

speaker: Unknown
en: The manager was a fantastic trainer.
zh: 那位经理是一位出色的培训师。

speaker: Unknown
en: He used to invite us out to his house nearly every Sunday to play ping pong, to eat, and to talk business.
zh: 他几乎每个星期天都邀请我们去他家打乒乓球、吃饭、聊生意。

speaker: Unknown
en: You could learn a lot.
zh: 你能学到很多东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: He was a manager who had a 25% bonus contract.
zh: 他是一位签有 25% 奖金合同的经理。

speaker: Unknown
en: He got his check.
zh: 他拿到了他的支票。

speaker: Unknown
en: Keep in mind, this is 1940.
zh: 记住，这是 1940 年。

speaker: Unknown
en: He waved that around one Sunday.
zh: 有一个星期天他挥舞着那张支票。

speaker: Unknown
en: That just made us run faster and work harder.
zh: 那让我们跑得更快、干得更卖力。

speaker: Unknown
en: Sam Walton's training and what he learned there would eventually put a few billion dollars into his own cash registers.
zh: Sam Walton 在那里受到的训练和他学到的东西，最终会给他自己的收银机里带来几十亿美元。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so when he's 27, he decides to buy a franchise of a Ben Franklin five and dime store.
zh: 于是，27 岁时，他决定购买一家 Ben Franklin 五分一毛店的特许经营权。

speaker: Unknown
en: These are tiny stores.
zh: 这些都是很小的店。

speaker: Unknown
en: They cost about $25,000 at the time.
zh: 当时它们大约值 25,000 美元。

speaker: Unknown
en: His father-in-law lends him the $25,000 needed to secure the franchise.
zh: 他的岳父借给他获得特许经营权所需的 25,000 美元。

speaker: Unknown
en: And this store is in this remote farming town of Newport, Arkansas.
zh: 这家店位于阿肯色州纽波特这个偏远的农业小镇。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I love this description of Sam Walton in the very first days of his very first store.
zh: 我很喜欢这段对 Sam Walton 在他第一家店最初日子里的描述。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is something he carries on throughout his entire life.
zh: 这是他贯穿一生都在坚持的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: He says, even in Newport, Sam Walton worked all of the hours.
zh: 书里说，即使在纽波特，Sam Walton 也是全天候工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: One of my favorite, I was watching this interview with Michael Dell, who's one of my personal heroes and someone I get to luckily spend time and speak to.
zh: 我最喜欢的一段之一，是我看过 Michael Dell 的一个访谈，他是我个人的英雄之一，也是我有幸能共度时光并交谈的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the interviewer asked Michael Dell, it's like, well, when you started your first company, like, what was your schedule like?
zh: 采访者问 Michael Dell，差不多是这样，当你创办你的第一家公司时，你的日程安排是什么样的？

speaker: Unknown
en: How many hours did you work?
zh: 你每周工作多少小时？

speaker: Unknown
en: And Michael says something hilarious.
zh: Michael 说了句特别好笑的话。

speaker: Unknown
en: He goes, all of them.
zh: 他说，全都要。

speaker: Unknown
en: So it's, again, very similar here.
zh: 所以这里又非常相似。

speaker: Unknown
en: Sam Walton worked all of the hours.
zh: Sam Walton 一天到晚都在工作。

zh: 我最近读了很多关于 SpaceX 的东西。

zh: SpaceX 是世界上最有价值的公司之一。

zh: 而 SpaceX 历史上的一个主要主题，就是不断攻击和质疑你的成本。

zh: 所以当你在用 RAMP 运营你的公司而你的竞争对手没有时，你就拥有一个随时间不断复利的巨大竞争优势。

zh: 有很多半成品式的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it says it was still largely a seat of the pants instinct of Sam Walton that guided his Walmart expansion.
zh: 书中说,引导他的 Walmart 扩张的,在很大程度上仍然是 Sam Walton 凭直觉的即兴判断。

speaker: Unknown
en: There was a lot of rough edges.
zh: 有很多粗糙的地方。

speaker: Unknown
en: They talk about the eighth Walmart ever.
zh: 他们谈到了有史以来第八家 Walmart。

speaker: Unknown
en: They didn't have a lot of resources, which I've mentioned a few times.
zh: 他们没有多少资源,这一点我已经提过几次了。

speaker: Unknown
en: So they have to take over.
zh: 所以他们不得不接手。

speaker: Unknown
en: The eighth Walmart ever was this old Coca-Cola bottling plant that had went out of business.
zh: 有史以来第八家 Walmart 是一家已经倒闭的老可口可乐装瓶厂。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it had all these pipes sticking out of the floor.
zh: 那里有各种管子从地板上伸出来。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so you had to stack all your inventory and what the customers would eventually buy around these pipes and all these drains.
zh: 所以你不得不把所有库存以及顾客最终要买的东西堆在这些管子和各种排水口周围。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the building also didn't even have any air conditioning.
zh: 而且那栋楼甚至没有空调。

speaker: Unknown
en: So they go out and buy 28 window fans.
zh: 所以他们出去买了 28 台窗式风扇。

speaker: Unknown
en: And in the late 60s, he's having a hard time financing the expansion.
zh: 到了 60 年代末,他在为扩张融资方面遇到了困难。

speaker: Unknown
en: He feels he's got the concept down, but they're moving too slow.
zh: 他觉得自己已经把模式搞明白了,但他们的扩张速度太慢。

speaker: Unknown
en: Walmart's eventually going to go public in 1970.
zh: Walmart 最终会在 1970 年上市。

speaker: Unknown
en: Before that, they're borrowing money from banks.
zh: 在那之前,他们从银行借钱。

speaker: Unknown
en: They're borrowing for a life insurance company.
zh: 他们从一家人寿保险公司借钱。

speaker: Unknown
en: So he's pitching this life insurance company.
zh: 所以他在向这家保险公司做推介。

speaker: Unknown
en: And again, I think this is absolutely nuts that he kind of nails down the future sales growth of Walmart.
zh: 再说一次,我觉得他基本上把 Walmart 未来的销售增长给敲定了,这实在是疯了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so Sam Walton is sitting across from this insurance company trying to get money.
zh: 于是 Sam Walton 坐在这家保险公司对面,想要拿到钱。

speaker: Unknown
en: And they're saying, hey, so your sales volume is around $20 million, right?
zh: 他们说:"嘿,你的销售额大概在 2000 万美元左右,对吧?"

speaker: Unknown
en: And Sam goes, yes, our business is really growing.
zh: Sam 说:"是的,我们的业务增长得非常快。

speaker: Unknown
en: For the fiscal year 1969, we did 21 million.
zh: 1969 财年,我们做到了 2100 万。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's quite a jump because the year before we only did 12 million.
zh: 这是个很大的跳跃,因为前一年我们只做了 1200 万。"

speaker: Unknown
en: And so they ask him, what do you think your sales volume will be five years from now?
zh: 于是他们问他:"你觉得五年后你的销售额会是多少?"

speaker: Unknown
en: And Sam says, our calculation is that in 1975, our sales volume will be 230 million.
zh: Sam 说:"我们计算的是,到 1975 年,我们的销售额将是 2.3 亿。"

speaker: Unknown
en: And they respond, what?
zh: 他们回应道:"什么?"

speaker: Unknown
en: The people from the insurance company were very skeptical.
zh: 保险公司的人非常怀疑。

speaker: Unknown
en: Sam Walton, however, was right on target.
zh: 然而,Sam Walton 完全正中目标。

speaker: Unknown
en: Total sales for 1975 came to 236 million.
zh: 1975 年的总销售额达到了 2.36 亿。

speaker: Unknown
en: That is nuts.
zh: 这简直疯了。

speaker: Unknown
en: So now he's got a working system, he's got way more capital, and he's public now.
zh: 所以现在他有了一套运转中的系统，他拥有的资本多得多，而且他现在已经上市了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And he's pushing the pace.
zh: 他在加快节奏。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is also where they talk about over and over again that he just churns through executives and he just pushed his top executives really hard.
zh: 这里他们还反复谈到，他不停地更换高管，而且他对顶尖高管的要求非常严苛。

speaker: Unknown
en: Sam was aware of the Walmart lifestyle.
zh: Sam 了解沃尔玛式生活方式的影响。

speaker: Unknown
en: He was alert to its dangers, the risk of burnout.
zh: 他对其危险性保持着警惕，即过度疲劳的风险。

speaker: Unknown
en: Sam had seen others resign or get fired because of the rigors of working in a pressure cooker for a boss that some staffers called that old slave driver.
zh: Sam 曾见过别人辞职或被解雇，都是因为在为一个压力锅般严苛的老板工作的艰辛所致——一些员工称那个老板为老监工。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so the people working with him also point out, yeah, he's got this like folksy, you know, charming country boy exterior, but you're missing what's actually underneath all that.
zh: 和他共事的人也指出，是的，他有一种乡巴佬式的、你知道吗、很有魅力的乡下小伙外表，但你可能没看到这一切之下真正的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: So it says he also claims that the public conception of Sam as a good old country boy wearing a soft velvet glove misses the fact that there's an iron fist within that glove.
zh: 所以书里说，他还声称，公众把 Sam 看作一个戴着天鹅绒手套的善良乡下小伙，却忽略了一个事实：那只手套里面藏着一双铁拳。

speaker: Unknown
en: Sam Walton is not one to stay still.
zh: Sam Walton 不是那种安于现状的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is what Sam says.
zh: 这就是 Sam 说的。

speaker: Unknown
en: I guess I can get a little tough if I see things that I don't like.
zh: 我想，如果我看到我不喜欢的事情，我会变得有点强硬。

speaker: Unknown
en: He stressed though that he knew his business from top to bottom.
zh: 不过他强调，他对自己的生意从头到尾都了如指掌。

speaker: Unknown
en: I used to do it all.
zh: 我曾经什么都干。

speaker: Unknown
en: Sweep the floor, keep the books, buy the merchandise.
zh: 扫地、记账、进货。

speaker: Unknown
en: One of my assets is my willingness to try something new, to change.
zh: 我的资产之一就是我愿意尝试新事物、愿意改变。

speaker: Unknown
en: That is a concept we carry throughout the company.
zh: 这是我们在整个公司贯彻的一个理念。

speaker: Unknown
en: The idea of changing course when you get new information was so important to him that he would repeat it throughout the entire company.
zh: 当你获得新信息时就改变方向，这个想法对他如此重要，以至于他会在整个公司反复强调。

speaker: Unknown
en: He would call it RC.
zh: 他会称之为 RC。

speaker: Unknown
en: You need to have a low RC, which is resistance to change.
zh: 你需要有低的 RC，也就是对变化的抗拒。

speaker: Unknown
en: We have a low resistance to change.
zh: 我们对变化的抗拒度很低。

speaker: Unknown
en: We call it our RC factor.
zh: 我们称之为我们的 RC 因素。

speaker: Unknown
en: And another interesting thing is as hard as he was on his executive, he seems to be, in the other direction, super supportive of the frontline workers and the people actually serving the customers.
zh: 另一件有趣的事是，尽管他对自己的高管如此严厉，但在另一个方向上，他似乎对一线员工以及真正服务顾客的人超级支持。

speaker: Unknown
en: And you see stories over and over again.
zh: 你会一遍又一遍地看到这样的故事。

speaker: Unknown
en: So one time, Sam's on the road, he sees one of his semi-trucks, he flags it down.
zh: 有一次，Sam 在路上，看到他的一辆半挂卡车，他把车拦了下来。

speaker: Unknown
en: He jumps into the cab and rides a hundred miles with the driver to gain firsthand experience that might improve Walmart's transportation.
zh: 他跳进驾驶室，和司机一起行驶了一百英里，以获得可能改进沃尔玛运输业务的第一手经验。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's other stories of him showing up at 2.30 in the morning, buying a bunch of donuts and taking them over to his warehouse where they're doing a loading dock for all of the inventory.
zh: 还有其他故事，比如他凌晨两点半出现，买了一大堆甜甜圈，带到他的仓库，那里正在为所有库存装货。

speaker: Unknown
en: And he would sit there and solicit ideas from the dock workers for how to upgrade their efforts.
zh: 他会坐在那里，向码头工人征集改进他们工作的想法。

speaker: Unknown
en: And in some cases, they'd be like, oh, you know, we could really use an extra shower or two.
zh: 有时他们会说，哦，你知道，我们真的需要一两个额外的淋浴间。

speaker: Unknown
en: And he'd immediately get them whatever they asked for.
zh: 而他会立刻给他们所要求的任何东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: And this is where he's spending most of his time.
zh: 而且这就是他大部分时间花的地方。

speaker: Unknown
en: He's not hanging out in the office.
zh: 他不是待在办公室里。

speaker: Unknown
en: He's in the stores.
zh: 他在门店里。

speaker: Unknown
en: He's in the warehouses.
zh: 他在仓库里。

speaker: Unknown
en: He's riding along with the truck drivers.
zh: 他和卡车司机一起跑车。

speaker: Unknown
en: So when Sam discusses his management style, he's dead serious about identifying it as MBWA, management by walking around.
zh: 所以当 Sam 谈论他的管理风格时，他会非常严肃地把它定义为 MBWA，即走动式管理。

speaker: Unknown
en: It means his tactic of haunting stores, which means not only his own stores, but his competitors' stores as well.
zh: 这意味着他巡逛门店的策略，不仅是他自己的门店，也包括竞争对手的门店。

speaker: Unknown
en: He's on the lookout for methods and means, the winning and losing tricks of mass merchandising.
zh: 他在寻找方法和手段，即大众商品零售中获胜和失败的诀窍。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then this goes back to the fact that, yeah, he's got a velvet glove, but he's got an iron fist within it.
zh: 而这又回到了那个事实：是的，他有一只天鹅绒手套，但手套里面有一双铁拳。

speaker: Unknown
en: The other side of the coin is Sam's toughness in dealing with merchandise salesmen who he calls vendors, and likewise with his own buyers who are charged with never failing to obtain rock bottom wholesale prices.
zh: 硬币的另一面是 Sam 在与商品推销员打交道时的强硬——他称他们为 vendor（供应商），同样，对他自己的采购员也是如此，这些采购员的职责是从不失败地拿到最底价的批发价格。

speaker: Unknown
en: At Sam's insistence, his buyers have demanded price concessions.
zh: 在 Sam 的坚持下，他的采购员会要求价格让步。

speaker: Unknown
en: Promising high volume sales from the biggest names in manufacturing, including P&G, General Electric, and Sony.
zh: 向制造业中最响亮的品牌承诺高销量，包括 P&G、通用电气和索尼。

speaker: Unknown
en: And this is a description of what it's like to be on the other side of these buyers.
zh: 这里有一段描述，讲的是站在这些采购员对面是什么感觉。

speaker: Unknown
en: These people are folksy and down to earth as homegrown tomatoes.
zh: 这些人像自家种的西红柿一样朴实、接地气。

speaker: Unknown
en: But when you start dealing with them, when you get past that down home and Bentonville business, they're hard as nails and every bit as sharp.
zh: 但当你开始和他们打交道时，当你越过那种乡土气和本顿维尔式的做派之后，他们硬得像钉子一样，而且同样精明。

speaker: Unknown
en: And one of the things they're excessively sharp about is having the lowest cost structure of anybody in their industry.
zh: 而他们极其精明的事情之一，就是拥有其行业中任何人之中最低的成本结构。

speaker: Unknown
en: In fact, let me read one of my favorite sentences from his autobiography before I get to this sentence in this book, which is about the importance of watching your costs.
zh: 事实上，在讲到这本书里的这句话之前，让我先读一段我最喜欢的、来自他的自传里的句子，是关于监控你的成本的重要性。

speaker: Unknown
en: Sam Walton writes, control your expenses better than your competition.
zh: Sam Walton 写道：比你的竞争对手更好地控制你的开支。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is where you can always find your competitive advantage.
zh: 这就是你总能找到你竞争优势的地方。

speaker: Unknown
en: We rank number one in our industry for the lowest ratio of expenses to sales.
zh: 我们在行业中排名第一，拥有最低的费用与销售额之比。

speaker: Unknown
en: In this book, it says Walmart boasts that their total administrative cost amounts to 2% of revenue.
zh: 在这本书里，它说沃尔玛夸耀他们的总行政成本只占收入的 2%。

speaker: Unknown
en: Far below industry norms.
zh: 远低于行业规范。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then we go back to this idea that number one, he's always recruiting, and that two, he would pitch the same person over and over and over again.
zh: 然后我们回到这个观点：第一，他一直在招人；第二，他会一次又一次、一次又一次地向同一个人推销。

speaker: Unknown
en: Someone said Sam Walton used up men the way he threw wood into his fireplace.
zh: 有人说，山姆·沃尔顿用人就像往壁炉里扔柴火一样。

speaker: Unknown
en: Just like the logs, they blazed up with a fury, generated powerful and beautifully efficient flames, and after a time died down into cold ashes.
zh: 就像那些木柴，熊熊燃烧，产生强大而美丽的高效火焰，过一段时间后熄灭成冷灰。

speaker: Unknown
en: It was necessary for him always to be looking to replenish his stockpile of talent.
zh: 对他来说，不断寻找补充人才储备是必要的。

speaker: Unknown
en: He fell back on his old habit of going after somebody who had already turned him down before.
zh: 他又回到老习惯，去追那些以前拒绝过他的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then we go back to his idea of, hey, I want to make sure I have a low resistance to change, even at 61, which is, you know, he's been running, now he's been in retail for four decades at this point.
zh: 然后我们回到他的想法：嘿，我要确保自己对变革的阻力很低，即使在61岁的时候，要知道，他到现在已经做零售四十年了。

speaker: Unknown
en: He's willing to listen to new information to change his mind.
zh: 他愿意倾听新信息来改变自己的想法。

speaker: Unknown
en: So at first, this is 1979, okay?
zh: 那么一开始，这是1979年，好吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: So at first...
zh: 所以一开始……

speaker: Unknown
en: Other executives in Walmart are telling about the importance of computers, that maybe we can use this, we can have an advantage.
zh: 沃尔玛的其他高管在告诉他计算机的重要性，也许我们可以利用它，我们可以获得优势。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's a very old idea.
zh: 这是一个非常古老的想法。

speaker: Unknown
en: The first time this really clicked for me is when I read Andrew Carnegie's autobiography, I don't know, like seven years ago.
zh: 这个想法第一次真正让我印象深刻，是大概七年前我读安德鲁·卡内基的自传的时候。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it's invest in technology, the savings compound.
zh: 那就是：投资于技术，节省会复利增长。

speaker: Unknown
en: It gives you an advantage over your slower moving competitors and can be the difference between a profit and a loss.
zh: 它让你比行动迟缓的竞争对手更有优势，可能就是盈利与亏损之间的差别。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so when his executives were first pitching Sam Walton to invest heavily into computers, he thought it was just overhead.
zh: 所以当他的高管第一次向山姆·沃尔顿推销要大量投资计算机时，他认为那只是开销。

speaker: Unknown
en: But then he listened, he learned, and then changed his mind and his course.
zh: 但后来他倾听了、学习了，然后改变了想法和方向。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then he goes in big.
zh: 然后他大举投入。

speaker: Unknown
en: He spends half a billion dollars in 1979 on this new computer system.
zh: 1979年，他在这套新计算机系统上花了五亿美元。

speaker: Unknown
en: Finally, his lieutenants educated to convince Sam and Walmart spent $500 million.
zh: 最终，他的副手们说服了山姆，沃尔玛花了五亿美元。

speaker: Unknown
en: So it's this computer system that's going to link the Walmart stores, warehouses, and distribution centers.
zh: 就是这套计算机系统，它将把沃尔玛的门店、仓库和配送中心连接起来。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so it says now the stores and warehouses communicate around the clock with headquarters.
zh: 于是书里说，现在门店和仓库全天候与总部沟通。

speaker: Unknown
en: They would get daily sales from the 36 departments in each store, bank deposits, estimated sales figures, reports on hot selling items and warehouse inventory.
zh: 他们会收到每家门店36个部门的每日销售额、银行存款、预估销售数字、热销商品报告和仓库库存情况。

speaker: Unknown
en: In the 1979 Walmart annual report, Sam wrote the financial savings and the number of person hours saved daily by using the computer center.
zh: 在1979年沃尔玛年报中，山姆写道，使用计算机中心每天节省的资金和节省的人工小时数

speaker: Unknown
en: Or incalculable, even by the computer.
zh: 连计算机本身都无法计算。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then he goes back to his idea.
zh: 然后他又回到他的想法。

speaker: Unknown
en: Once he knew something was working, he was intolerant of slowness in expanding that.
zh: 一旦他知道某件事行得通，他就无法容忍在扩张这件事上的迟缓。

speaker: Unknown
en: So it says Walmart was growing too slowly to suit Sam.
zh: 书里说，沃尔玛的增长对山姆来说太慢了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Anyone but Sam might have been satisfied with his company's progress.
zh: 换成除山姆以外的任何人，可能都会对公司的进展感到满意。

speaker: Unknown
en: So between 1974 and 1977.
zh: 在1974年到1977年之间。

speaker: Unknown
en: Okay, so three years, they go from 78 to 153 stores and from sales of 167 million to $478 million.
zh: 好的，三年时间，他们从78家店增长到153家店，销售额从1.67亿美元增长到4.78亿美元。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so Sam can't figure out how to grow any faster organically.
zh: 而山姆想不出如何更快地自然增长。

speaker: Unknown
en: So then he starts doing acquisitions.
zh: 于是他开始做收购。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so there'll be like a chain of say, like 16 other stores.
zh: 比如会有一个大约16家店的其他连锁店。

speaker: Unknown
en: He'll buy them and then convert those 16 stores into Walmarts.
zh: 他会买下来，然后把那16家店改造成沃尔玛。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so he discovers, hey, I'm only able to make two to three at this point in his career, only two to three my own, but I can buy 16 in one fell swoop.
zh: 于是他发现，嘿，在他职业生涯的这个阶段，他自己一年只能开两到三家店，但我可以一举买下16家。

speaker: Unknown
en: I can move a lot faster.
zh: 我可以走得快得多。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then he goes and targets bigger retail like chains.
zh: 然后他开始瞄准更大的零售连锁。

speaker: Unknown
en: At one point, he buys this one retail chain that has 104 stores and then converts all 104 stores into Walmarts.
zh: 有一次，他买下了一家拥有104家店的零售连锁，然后把全部104家店都改造成沃尔玛。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then a few pages later, he goes back to this.
zh: 然后在几页之后，他又回到这一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is a trademark of ours.
zh: 这是我们的一个标志。

speaker: Unknown
en: We are willing to change.
zh: 我们愿意改变。

speaker: Unknown
en: Every day is a different situation in the retail business.
zh: 在零售业，每天都是不同的局面。

speaker: Unknown
en: We have been very flexible and have been looking every day for changes that need to be made.
zh: 我们一直非常灵活，每天都在寻找需要做出的改变。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so there's all these great stories that spread throughout the book where just Sam's constantly collecting info from the front lines.
zh: 书里散布着所有这些精彩的故事，山姆不断地从前线收集信息。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so one of his friend's daughters has a bad experience in a Walmart.
zh: 他一个朋友的女儿在沃尔玛有一次糟糕的经历。

speaker: Unknown
en: She buys a pair of shorts.
zh: 她买了一条短裤。

speaker: Unknown
en: They weren't the right size.
zh: 尺码不对。

speaker: Unknown
en: So then she goes back to the store.
zh: 于是她回到那家店。

speaker: Unknown
en: They didn't have the right size to exchange.
zh: 店里没有合适的尺码可以换。

speaker: Unknown
en: She's like, OK, let me just get my money back.
zh: 她说,好吧,我只要把我的钱拿回来。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the manager wouldn't give it.
zh: 经理不肯给。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so he's telling the story where he's at this party with the Waltons, Sam Walton and his wife, and his daughter calls and he puts Sam on the phone.
zh: 于是他讲了这么一个故事:他在一个聚会上和沃尔顿一家在一起,就是 Sam Walton 和他的妻子,然后他女儿打来电话,他把电话递给了 Sam。

speaker: Unknown
en: So he says, we're at this bridge party with the Waltons and my daughter wanted to speak to Sam.
zh: 所以他说,我们正在和沃尔顿一家参加这个桥牌聚会,我女儿想和 Sam 说几句话。

speaker: Unknown
en: He got on the phone and listened.
zh: 他接过电话,倾听着。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then Sam calls the manager, talked to the manager for a bit and then hung up.
zh: 然后 Sam 打电话给那位经理,和经理谈了一会儿,然后挂断了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then the manager got awfully nice and gave the money back.
zh: 接着经理变得特别客气,把钱退了回去。

speaker: Unknown
en: Not long after that, Sam and I were talking and I said I wanted to apologize for my daughter calling while we had a party.
zh: 那之后不久,Sam 和我在聊天,我说我想为我女儿在聚会时打电话过来道歉。

speaker: Unknown
en: And he said, oh no, I'm glad she called.
zh: 他说,哦不,我很高兴她打了电话。

speaker: Unknown
en: Boy, that's been its weight in gold.
zh: 天哪,这件事的价值抵得上它的重量换成的黄金。

speaker: Unknown
en: I told the manager that I wanted him to bring that pair of shorts to our Saturday morning meeting.
zh: 我告诉那位经理,我要他把那条短裤带到我们周六早晨的会议上。

speaker: Unknown
en: I made him stand up and hold up those shorts.
zh: 我让他站起来,把那条短裤举起来。

speaker: Unknown
en: Then I asked him, what is our motto?
zh: 然后我问他,我们的口号是什么?

speaker: Unknown
en: And he said, satisfaction guaranteed.
zh: 他说,保证满意。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, every once in a while, you have to refresh their memory.
zh: 你知道,每隔一段时间,你就得帮他们刷新一下记忆。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so this is one of my favorite Sam Walton stories.
zh: 所以这是我最喜欢的 Sam Walton 故事之一。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is what I was mentioning earlier is like, remember that he worked on one, a single store for the first five and a half years of his career.
zh: 这就是我前面提到的:记住,他职业生涯的头五年半只经营一家店,就一家店。

speaker: Unknown
en: Look how fast he's able to go later on in his career.
zh: 再看看他职业生涯后期走得有多快。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is when he copies SoulPrice.
zh: 这就是他抄 SoulPrice 的时候。

speaker: Unknown
en: I've done a few episodes on SoulPrice.
zh: 我做过几期关于 SoulPrice 的节目。

speaker: Unknown
en: SoulPrice is probably the most influential retailer has ever lived.
zh: SoulPrice 可能是有史以来最有影响力的零售商。

speaker: Unknown
en: Sam Walton said he stole more ideas from SoulPrice than anybody else.
zh: Sam Walton 说他从 SoulPrice 那里偷的创意比从任何其他人那里都多。

speaker: Unknown
en: Jeff Bezos got ideas from SoulPrice.
zh: Jeff Bezos 的创意也来自 SoulPrice。

speaker: Unknown
en: Jim Sinegal, the founder of Costco, was mentored by SoulPrice.
zh: Jim Sinegal,Costco 的创始人,是被 SoulPrice 指导过的。

speaker: Unknown
en: The Home Depot concept, Bernie Marcus got that idea from SoulPrice.
zh: Home Depot 这个概念,Bernie Marcus 就是从 SoulPrice 那里得到的灵感。

speaker: Unknown
en: So SoulPrice is, again, maybe like the general population aren't aware of who he was.
zh: 所以 SoulPrice,再说一次,普通大众可能不知道他是谁。

speaker: Unknown
en: But if you were in retail, you damn sure studied him.
zh: 但如果你在零售业,你绝对研究过他。

speaker: Unknown
en: And Sam Walton did so, too.
zh: Sam Walton 也是如此。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it winds up, as a result of this, creating one of the most valuable lines, like this extension into
zh: 结果就是,这最终催生出了最有价值的业务线之一,像这样的一次延伸,

speaker: Unknown
en: From Walmart into Sam's Club.
zh: 从 Walmart 延伸到 Sam's Club。

speaker: Unknown
en: And this is happening in the 1980s.
zh: 而这发生在 20 世纪 80 年代。

speaker: Unknown
en: Listen to the story.
zh: 听听这个故事。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's excellent.
zh: 非常精彩。

speaker: Unknown
en: On a sunny January morning in 1983, Sam Walton flew into San Diego to investigate a new wrinkle in the discount business, a membership wholesale club.
zh: 1983 年 1 月一个阳光明媚的早晨,Sam Walton 飞抵圣地亚哥,去调查折扣零售业的一个新花样:会员制仓储俱乐部。

speaker: Unknown
en: The idea was originated five years earlier by a savvy California entrepreneur named Sol Price.
zh: 这个点子是五年前由一位精明的加州企业家提出的,他叫 Sol Price。

speaker: Unknown
en: Sol Price was making an astounding success by selling merchandise at only 10% above manufacturing prices and getting rich.
zh: Sol Price 只以高于制造成本 10% 的价格出售商品,却获得了惊人的成功,并且发了财。

speaker: Unknown
en: If Sol Price could do that, Sam Walton figured he could do it too.
zh: Sam Walton 心想,如果 Sol Price 能做到,他也能做到。

speaker: Unknown
en: Sam intended to borrow from Sol Price just as he had copied schemes originated by JCPenney, Herb Gibson, and many other good merchants.
zh: Sam 打算从 Sol Price 那里借鉴,就像他曾照搬 JCPenney、Herb Gibson 以及许多其他优秀商人的做法一样。

speaker: Unknown
en: The wholesale club idea was good.
zh: 仓储俱乐部这个点子很好。

speaker: Unknown
en: It was extraordinary good.
zh: 好得不得了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Sam returned to Bentonville and called together his top strategists.
zh: Sam 回到本顿维尔,召集起他的顶级战略家们。

speaker: Unknown
en: Walton hopped on this new scheme with enthusiasm.
zh: Walton 满腔热情地投入了这个新做法。

speaker: Unknown
en: Brashly copying from sole price, Walton began creating a division of Sam's Wholesale Clubs.
zh: 大胆地照搬 sole price,Walton 开始创建 Sam's Wholesale Clubs 这个部门。

speaker: Unknown
en: For years, Walton had been seeking some effective way to get his everyday low price methods and concepts into the rich and sophisticated metropolitan markets and now he had finally found it.
zh: 多年来,Walton 一直在寻找某种有效方式,把他「天天低价」的方法和理念带进富裕而成熟的都市市场,而现在他终于找到了。

speaker: Unknown
en: New Sam's Clubs were opened rapidly.
zh: 新的 Sam's Club 迅速开张。

speaker: Unknown
en: By the end of 1983, three clubs were up and running.
zh: 到 1983 年底,已有三家俱乐部开张运营。

speaker: Unknown
en: Eight more clubs opened in 1984.
zh: 1984 年又开了八家。

speaker: Unknown
en: In 1985, he opened 12 more.
zh: 1985 年,他又开了 12 家。

speaker: Unknown
en: By the end of that year, he had 23 clubs doing $776 million in sales.
zh: 到那一年年底,他拥有 23 家俱乐部,销售额达 7.76 亿美元。

speaker: Unknown
en: By 1990, Walton had 105 of these wholesale clubs in operation with annual sales in excess of $5 billion.
zh: 到 1990 年,Walton 拥有 105 家这样的仓储俱乐部在运营,年销售额超过 50 亿美元。

speaker: Unknown
en: So think about that.
zh: 想想这一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: For the first five and a half years of his career, he had a single store.
zh: 在他职业生涯的前五年半里，他只有一家店。

speaker: Unknown
en: Later on,
zh: 后来，

speaker: Unknown
en: In a seven-year period, he's able to start 105 stores of a new concept and get to $5 billion in sales.
zh: 在七年的时间里，他能够创办 105 家新概念的门店，销售额达到 50 亿美元。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then this is probably one of his best ideas.
zh: 而这可能是他最好的点子之一。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's certainly surprising.
zh: 这当然令人惊讶。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it's just another example of Sam copying good ideas.
zh: 这只是 Sam 抄袭好点子的又一个例子。

speaker: Unknown
en: So it says, for when and how and why he and his wife shared their business resources with their four children is one of the more fascinating untold Walton episodes.
zh: 书里说，他和他妻子是何时以及如何、为什么把他们的商业资源分享给四个孩子的，这是 Walton 家最引人入胜的未讲述的篇章之一。

speaker: Unknown
en: The children have each owned one fifth of their parents' stock and property since 1954.
zh: 补充：Sam 和 Helen 设立这个信托时，Ron 才 10 岁，Alice 只有 5 岁。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think at the time he gave them stock, I think it was worth something like $5,000 if I remember correctly.
zh: 我想当时他给他们的股票，如果我没记错的话，价值大约 5,000 美元。

speaker: Unknown
en: Sam and Helen created the trust that set this up when Ron was 10 and Alice was only five.
zh: Sam 和 Helen 在 Ron 十岁、Alice 才五岁时设立了这项信托。

speaker: Unknown
en: Doing this kind of estate planning so early in the game was urged on Sam by his father-in-law, L.S.
zh: 这么早做这种遗产规划，是 Sam 的岳父 L.S.

speaker: Unknown
en: Robson, who had earlier done precisely the same thing in giving Helen and her siblings equal shares in a vast ranch that he owned in Oklahoma.
zh: Robson 劝他做的，Robson 之前做过完全一样的事，把他位于俄克拉荷马州的一片大牧场平均分给了 Helen 和她的兄弟姐妹。

speaker: Unknown
en: Mr. Robson was a banker and a lawyer and pretty smart, Sam once explained.
zh: Sam 曾解释说，Robson 先生是银行家也是律师，相当聪明。

speaker: Unknown
en: I could see it was the thing to do.
zh: 我看得出来这是该做的事。

speaker: Unknown
en: And this all took place four decades ago.
zh: 而这一切发生在四十年前。

speaker: Unknown
en: I came home and had the papers drawn up.
zh: 我回家后让人把文件拟好了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And one of his sons talks about this.
zh: 他的一个儿子谈到过这件事。

speaker: Unknown
en: At the time, all dad and mom had was a variety store or two.
zh: 那时候，爸爸妈妈拥有的只是一两家杂货店。

speaker: Unknown
en: Our shares couldn't have been worth more than $5,000 each.
zh: 我们的股份当时每份不可能超过 5,000 美元。

speaker: Unknown
en: It has been Sam's imagination, genius, and drive that has exploded these shares to a value of almost $2 billion each.
zh: 是 Sam 的想象力、天赋和干劲把这些股份爆炸式地增值到了每份将近 20 亿美元。

speaker: Unknown
en: And at the time of recording this, those shares, depending on the child, are worth somewhere between $130 billion, $127 billion, and $117 billion.
zh: 而在录制这期节目的时候，那些股份，取决于哪个孩子，价值大约在 1,300 亿、1,270 亿和 1,170 亿美元之间。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then I'll close with one of my favorite stories about Sam Walton's relentless focus on work.
zh: 最后我用一个我最喜欢的关于 Sam Walton 对工作不懈专注的故事来收尾。

speaker: Unknown
en: This has to do with the Wall Street crash of October 1987.
zh: 这和 1987 年 10 月的华尔街股灾有关。

speaker: Unknown
en: It is one of my all time favorite Sam Walton stories.
zh: 这是我有史以来最喜欢的 Sam Walton 的故事之一。

speaker: Unknown
en: Stock market crashes, says the day the market dropped 500 points and knocked a billion dollars off the value of his stock holdings in Walmart.
zh: 股市崩盘，据说那天市场下跌了 500 点，使他在 Walmart 的股票持仓蒸发了十亿美元。

speaker: Unknown
en: Reporters asked Sam what his reaction to the disaster on Wall Street was.
zh: 记者问 Sam 对华尔街这场灾难的反应是什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: He hadn't heard about it.
zh: 他根本没听说过这件事。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that is where I'll leave it.
zh: 我就讲到这里。

speaker: Unknown
en: Highly recommend reading the book.
zh: 强烈推荐读这本书。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you haven't read Sam's autobiography, I would start with that first.
zh: 如果你还没读过 Sam 的自传，我会先从那本开始。

speaker: Unknown
en: But if you had read Sam's autobiography, I would definitely buy this book.
zh: 但如果你已经读过 Sam 的自传，我肯定建议你买这本书。

speaker: Unknown
en: I will leave a link down below.
zh: 我会在下方留下链接。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you buy the book using that link, you'll be supporting podcasts at the same time.
zh: 如果你用那个链接买书，你同时也支持了播客。

speaker: Unknown
en: That is 434 books down, 1,000 to go.
zh: 这就是读完的第 434 本书，还剩 1,000 本。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I'll talk to you again soon.
zh: 我们很快会再聊。
